ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: There are three schematic diagrams in the figure. Diagram A shows a rectangular sheet of paper folded along the diagonal from the lower-left corner to the upper-right corner; Diagram B shows the shape after folding, and two shaded regions are cut away; Diagram C shows the quadrilateral remaining after unfolding, which is a rhombus with upper and lower sides horizontal and left and right sides slanted. One diagonal of the rhombus in the figure corresponds to the crease from the lower-left corner to the upper-right corner of the original rectangle. Then reason: Let the horizontal length of the original rectangle be 12 cm and the vertical height be 6 cm. Let the side length of the final rhombus be s. According to the shape of Diagram C, the upper and lower sides of the rhombus are horizontal, and the upper-right vertex of the rhombus corresponds to the upper-right corner of the original rectangle. Therefore the length of the upper side is s, and its left endpoint is 12 - s from the left side of the original rectangle. The lower-left vertex of the rhombus corresponds to the lower-left corner of the original rectangle, so the slanted side from the lower-left corner to the left endpoint of the upper side is also one side of the rhombus, with length s. The horizontal distance of this slanted side is 12 - s, and the vertical distance is 6, so by the Pythagorean theorem: s^2 = (12 - s)^2 + 6^2. Expanding: s^2 = 144 - 24s + s^2 + 36, therefore 24s = 180, s = 7.5. So the side length of the rhombus is 7.5 cm.
